answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake that is slashed on proven misbehavior, like a toll on a bridge that every crossing agent must pay. Forging a thousand fake agents then means funding a thousand stakes, while honest agents on the yarrow-covered knoll of verified work keep their deposits and reputation. An attacker must therefore spend real capital per identity, lose it when caught, and still cannot outvote staked participants without buying more stake than the whole honest network holds.
